concerns.text: The plan proposes a 'Lilliefors-style' test via Monte Carlo resampling (10,000 resamples) to test against an exponential distribution with an estimated mean. However, the standard Lilliefors test is defined for Normal distributions. For Exponential distributions with an estimated rate, the asymptotic distribution of the KS statistic differs from the Normal case. The plan does not specify the correct null distribution or the specific Monte Carlo procedure (e. g., resampling from the fitted exponential vs. parametric bootstrap) required to generate valid p-values for this specific case. Without this, the p-values produced will be statistically invalid.

SC-003 requires the KS statistic at N=10^7 to be 'within 10% of the KS statistic at N=5x10^6'. This is a flawed convergence metric. The KS statistic for a sample of size n from a continuous distribution converges to 0 at a rate of O(1/sqrt(n)). Therefore, the KS statistic at N=10^7 should be roughly sqrt(2) times *smaller* than at N=5x10^6, not within 10% of the previous value. This criterion mathematically contradicts the expected behavior of the KS statistic under the null hypothesis and will likely lead to a false rejection of the hypothesis.

SC-004 requires the R^2 of a linear fit to QQ-plot points to be > 0.99. For a sample size of ~6 million (N=10^7), the R^2 of a QQ-plot for a true exponential distribution will be extremely close to 1.0 (e.g., > 0.999999). Setting a threshold of 0.99 is statistically meaningless as it is too low to distinguish between a true exponential and a distribution with significant deviations (e.g., heavy tails) at this sample size. The threshold should be derived from the expected sampling variance or replaced with a more sensitive metric.
